question.leadin: Identify these longtime Senators who died in 2009 or 2010.
question.text: This longest-serving Senator in U.S. history represented West Virginia in the Senate from 1959 until his death in 2010.
question.clue: This long-serving West Virginian senator who once gave a 14-hour speech to filibuster the 1964 Civil Rights Act.

swap.text: In a tweet, this South Carolina senator stated that "any policy proposal which drives up costs of Corona, tequila, or margaritas is a big-time bad idea" in response to a 20% income tax with Mexico to pay the wall.
swap.clue: This Senator, who is widely rumored to be gay, has remained low in the polls but was widely regarded as the winner of the September 16th "kid's table" debate.

question.text: The first Jewish woman to serve on the Supreme Court, she served for 13 years on the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit before being nominated by Bill Clinton in 1993.
question.clue: This co-founder of the ACLU's Women's Rights Project struck down VMI's male-only admission policy as part of her longtime advocacy for women's rights.

swap.text: This man served as Governor of Florida from 1999-2007, becoming the first two-term Republican governor in the state's history. He is the son of a former US President and the brother of another.
swap.clue: Alex Sink, the Democrat defeated by Scott, now makes a historically unique household with her husband Bill McBride, who lost the 2002 Florida Gubernatorial election to this mentor of Marco Rubio.

question.leadin: Name some Democrats who will undoubtedly be squabbling onstage for the 2016 presidential nomination.
question.text: All signs point to this ex-Secretary of State and rival to Barack Obama in 2008 running, and winning the nomination.
question.clue: This politician's tearful speech at a campaign stop contributed to a comeback win in the 2008 New Hampshire primary.

swap.leadin: Identify these other United States Secretaries of State.
swap.text: She served for the second term of Bill Clinton's presidency, she was the first woman Secretary of State and was confirmed unanimously by the Senate
swap.clue: This successor to Warren Christopher converted to Catholicism in her childhood for safety from the Nazis while her father worked in the cabinet of Edvard Benes ("BEH-nesh").

question.text: During his reelection campaign in 1984, Reagan's team aired this optimistic advertisement. It presented the ways that life had gotten better under Reagan's presidency, comparing the present to the title time of day.
question.clue: The 1984 Reagan ad, "Prouder, Stronger, Better," which asks "Why would we ever want to return to where we were less than four short years ago?" is better known for opening with this line, which became his reelection slogan.

swap.text: One possible spoiler for Clinton's nomination is this man, the Democratic former governor of Maryland. His achievements as governor include the legalization of gay marriage and making some undocumented immigrants eligible for college tuition.
swap.clue: This governor of Maryland has publicly declared interest for the 2016 Democratic nomination. He signed a 2012 law legalizing same-sex marriage in his state.

question.text: Then Solicitor General, this conservative, who was rejected when Reagan tried to appoint him to the Supreme Court in 1987, carried out Nixon's orders and fired Cox.
question.clue: William Saxbe replaced him as acting Attorney General, a position he took on after the resignation of William Ruckelshaus.

swap.leadin: Identify these alums of Mount Holyoke.
swap.text: This 1975 alumna in economics became the first Asian-American woman appointed to a Cabinet position, namely Secretary of Labor by George W. Bush.
swap.clue: This Taiwan-born politician was the first Chinese American to be appointed to a President's Cabinet, serving as Secretary of Labour for the entire Bush Administration.

question.leadin: This judge wrote the majority opinion in Morse v. Frederick, which upheld a suspension from school for a student who displayed the banner "BONG HiTS 4 JESUS" outside of school.
question.text: Name this man who succeeded William Rehnquist in 2005 as Chief Justice.
question.clue: This man decided that the intent of the words "established by the State" was more important than their exact meaning, upholding federal exchanges.

swap.text: The sons of one of the founding John Birch Society members are these two brothers, who run a Kansas based conglomerate. They give lots of money to libertarian and conservative groups - particular, they were major donors to Scott Walker's campaign in Wisconsin.

question.leadin: Name some Republican 2008 nominees for president.
question.text: This senator from Kansas is a total redneck who advocates complete banning of abortion and a flat tax, and wants to "renew the family".
question.clue: This Republican Kansas governor was re-elected despite more than a hundred Republicans endorsing his Democratic opponent in response to this man's extensive, revenue-negative tax cuts.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about political scandals in the 1980s.
swap.text: This Senator from Colorado withdrew his campaign for the Democratic nomination shortly after photos were released of him and Donna Rice on a yacht named Monkey Business.
swap.clue: In his first campaign for his party's nomination, his opponent quoted a Wendy's commercial in asking him "Where's the beef?"

question.leadin: In order to calculate this metric for an election, net wasted votes are divided by the total number of votes cast.
question.text: Name this objective computer-implemented metric devised by law professor Nicholas Stephanopoulos and political scientist Eric McGhee to nullify the ability to gerrymander in a partisan fashion.
question.clue: One element of Gill lacking in previous gerrymandering cases is the use of this metric, which quantifies the number of "wasted votes" for each party. This metric was developed by Stephanopoulos and McGhee at UChicago.

swap.leadin: This legislation created the FBI's NICS background check system.
swap.text: Name this bill signed into law by Bill Clinton. It was named in honor of Ronald Reagan's press secretary who took a bullet during John Hinckley's attempted assassination of the president.
swap.answerHtml: Brady Bill [or Brady Act; or Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act]

question.text: This Supreme Court justice wrote majority opinions striking down moments of silence in Wallace v. Jaffree and prayer at football games in Santa Fe v. Doe. He replaced William O. Douglas on the bench in 1975.
question.clue: This Supreme Court justice who retired in 2010 and was replaced by Elena Kagan.

swap.text: In New Jersey, this female state senator is the most likely Democratic nominee to run against Republican Chris Christie.

swap.text: Although viewed by conservatives as a right-wing vote, Souter voted with the majority in this case, which ruled that schools could not sponsor clerics in even non-denominational prayers. This case dealt with a rabbi delivering a prayer at a graduation ceremony.
